title: AP reports rallies against Fico’s government across Slovakia on Velvet Revolution anniversary
summary: People rallied against Prime Minister Robert Fico’s government across Slovakia on the anniversary of the Velvet Revolution, according to the Associated Press. TASR reported that Fico urged fair political competition and said he hoped the opposition would not use public gatherings to spread hatred. The desk has not confirmed it.

sources.scope: Live reporting and photographs from protest locations
Reporting from Bratislava and remarks by protest participants

responses.text: According to TASR, Fico said he hoped the opposition would not use public gatherings to spread hatred and called for fair political competition.

title: Senate Democrats seek pause in air traffic control router replacements, AP reports
summary: According to AP, Senate Democrats asked Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy to pause air traffic control router replacements until the cause of the previous week's nationwide ground stop is established. A Transportation Department spokesperson told States Newsroom that the department had been transparent about the incident and would continue providing updates as they became available. The desk has not confirmed it.

sources.scope: A letter from Senate Democrats to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy; AP also obtained a separate administration funding-request letter.
Quotes the senators’ letter and cites Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy’s remarks.
Cites and links to the senators’ published letter and reports an email from a Transportation Department spokesperson to States Newsroom.

responses.text: According to States Newsroom, the spokesperson said the department had been transparent about the incident and would continue providing updates as they became available.

title: Apple reports iCloud sign-in outage as users report problems with other services
summary: Apple's system status page listed an iCloud Account & Sign In outage and said access could be slow or unavailable, according to Yahoo. Users also reported problems with services including the App Store and Apple Pay, according to 9to5Mac and Yahoo; those reports do not confirm separate outages. The desk has not confirmed it.

sources.scope: User reports of connection and sign-in failures.
Apple's outage notice and user reports.

responses.text: Apple's system status page listed an iCloud Account & Sign In outage and said the service could be slow or unavailable.

title: Apple status page listed account and service disruptions, MacRumors reports
summary: MacRumors reported that users had trouble signing in to Apple accounts and iCloud, and that Apple's status page listed issues affecting several services. The Daily Beast separately reported user disruptions, citing user reports and outage-monitoring information. The desk has not confirmed it.

sources.scope: Multiple social media reports and Apple's System Status page.
Reports of user disruptions and outage-monitoring information.

responses.text: According to MacRumors, Apple's system status page listed issues affecting iCloud Account and Sign In, followed by outages affecting the App Store, Apple Music and AppleCare on Device.

title: Apple says internal update caused outages affecting its online services
summary: The Associated Press reported that Apple attributed outages affecting services including the App Store, Apple Music and iCloud sign-ins to an internal update. Engadget reported observing service disruptions, while Apple told AP that many systems were back up and work continued to restore the remainder. The desk has not confirmed it.

sources.scope: Observed disruption affecting Apple services; published at 18:15 UTC.
Apple system status page and an emailed statement from Apple.
Apple service reports and a customer who visited a Philadelphia Apple store.

responses.text: Apple told the Associated Press that an internal update caused the outages, many systems were back up, and it was working to restore the remainder.

title: Trump Jr. and Kalshi say they agreed to end his advisory role
summary: Donald Trump Jr. told Axios that he and Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour agreed to end his advisory relationship with the company. Kalshi spokesperson Dani Lever told AP that the decision followed his firm’s significant investment in rival Polymarket. The desk has not confirmed it.

sources.scope: Interview with Donald Trump Jr. and comments from 1789 Capital partner Omeed Malik.
Kalshi spokesperson Dani Lever described the decision and its connection to 1789 Capital’s increased investment in Polymarket.
A Kalshi spokesperson confirmed the departure; Reuters also cited sources familiar with the matter.
A Kalshi spokesperson and company representatives described the mutual decision and the investment that prompted discussions.

responses.text: He told Axios that he and Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour discussed the advisory relationship and agreed to end it.
She told AP that Kalshi and Trump Jr. mutually agreed to end his advisory role after his firm’s significant investment in a competitor, and thanked him for helping market Kalshi.

title: White House withdrew Heidi Overton’s FDA nomination, AP reports
summary: The White House told AP it had withdrawn Heidi Overton’s nomination to lead the Food and Drug Administration. A senior administration official told Axios that Overton lacked sufficient support on Capitol Hill for confirmation and that the administration wanted a new direction at the FDA. The desk has not confirmed it.

sources.scope: A senior administration official.
The White House said it had pulled the nomination.

responses.who: Senior administration official, speaking to Axios
responses.text: The official said Overton lacked sufficient support on Capitol Hill for confirmation and that the administration needed a new direction at the FDA.

title: AP calls Alaska Senate race for Mary Peltola; CBS News independently projects her victory
summary: The Associated Press called Alaska’s U.S. Senate race for Democrat Mary Peltola over Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan, and CBS News independently projected her victory. Peltola said in a statement reported by AP that voters had signaled dissatisfaction with the status quo in DC. The desk has not confirmed it.

sources.scope: AP race call based on election results.
CBS News says it independently projects Peltola's victory. The available article was updated at 03:47 UTC.
NBC News made its own election projection; the article URL was identified through a separate election reference, but the article itself was inaccessible.

responses.text: In a statement reported by AP, Peltola said voters had signaled that the status quo in DC was not working for Alaska.

title: AP reports Iran war disruptions to regional sport as Qatar and Abu Dhabi F1 races remain scheduled
summary: The Associated Press reported that the Iran war has disrupted major sporting events across the Middle East. In an interview with The National, FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem said the federation was prepared for the Qatar and Abu Dhabi Formula 1 races to proceed. The desk has not confirmed it.

sources.scope: AP reporting and interviews with regional and sports researchers, including an analyst at the International Institute for Strategic Studies.
Exclusive interview with FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem.
Reports FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem's public statement and the disruption to earlier regional races.

Interviews Middle East researcher Kristian Ulrichsen and sports professor Simon Chadwick about disruption to regional events; says the Qatar and Abu Dhabi races remain scheduled but their staging is uncertain.

responses.text: Told The National that the FIA was ready and fully prepared for the Qatar and Abu Dhabi races to proceed.

title: AP: Garcia sends preservation letters ahead of planned House investigations into Trump administration
summary: AP reported that Representative Robert Garcia sent document-preservation letters to members of President Donald Trump's family and senior officials ahead of planned House investigations into the administration. White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis told WIRED that the president was willing to work with anyone to deliver results, while criticizing the proposed Democratic investigations. The desk has not confirmed it.

sources.scope: Letters released Wednesday and a statement from Garcia.
Describes and quotes multiple letters from Garcia, including their recipients and requests.
Describes and quotes Garcia's letters and obtained responses directly from a White House spokeswoman and a World Liberty spokesperson.

responses.text: Told WIRED that the president was willing to work with anyone to deliver results, but said Democrats pursuing investigations she characterized as shams would be working against the American people.
Told WIRED that congressional scrutiny of a company he described as compliant would be troubling without a basis.
WIRED reported that the representative did not immediately respond to its request for comment.
